source: Royal University of Agriculture student technical report on Alfalfa cultivation (Medicago sativa), referencing international agronomy sources (Utah State University, FAO, and others)
text: Land selection guidance emphasizes deep, well-drained soil, since alfalfa develops a long taproot system that penetrates deeply and is intolerant of waterlogged or shallow, poorly-drained soils — a compacted or high-water-table site will restrict root depth and shorten the stand's productive life. Climate discussion covers alfalfa's need for adequate soil moisture through establishment and its tolerance of a range of temperatures once established, drawing on international reference data rather than Cambodia-specific field trial results.
